channel.title: Main Street AI Brief
channel.description: Plain-English AI for small business owners: what works, what to avoid, and what it means for your shop.

item.title: Most small businesses use AI. Few feel confident with it.
item.description:
Bluehost's 2026 study of 350 U.S. small business owners found 87% use at least one AI tool, but only 20% describe themselves as highly confident. 30% name lack of AI knowledge as the main barrier, 27% say tools aren't specific to their type of business, and only 5% call cost their biggest concern.

So what: Your edge isn't buying more tools. It's learning to use one tool well on one real task.

Source: Bluehost, State of Small Business AI Confidence 2026

item.title: The barrier is expertise, not cost
item.description:
Bookipi surveyed 2,121 small business owners across 17 industries. Lack of expertise was the #1 challenge (32.1%), followed by unclear ROI (23.1%), integration (18.4%) and data privacy (12.3%). Marketing (36.2%) and customer service (36.1%) lead adoption; finance (16.4%), inventory (10.9%) and HR (6.4%) lag.

So what: Start where others already get value: customer replies and marketing drafts. Track minutes saved to answer the ROI question.

Source: Bookipi 2026 AI Adoption Report

item.title: Only 23% of small firms have a written AI policy
item.description:
Pax8's Q2 2026 Pulse report found only 23% of SMBs have a documented AI use policy; 28% have informal guidelines. Security or privacy concerns (23%) and lack of internal expertise (22%) are the top barriers to expanding AI use.

So what: A one-page rule sheet (what customer data never goes into AI, which tools are approved) protects you before a crew member pastes the wrong thing.

Source: Pax8 Pulse Report 2026 Q2
